text.p: Programme of matches in the German first division this weekend.

Bayer Leverkusen (2) vs Bochum (5). After just missing out on the championship, Leverkusen will have to summon all reserves of will to overcome Bochum, delighted to have won a UEFA cup place in their first season in the Bundesliga after promotion.
Fortuna Duesseldorf (16) vs Hamburg (15). With Duesseldorf already releguated and Hamburg having barely escaped the same fate, this game will be mainly about pride.
1860 Munich (6) vs Werder Bremen (8). A win here for 1860 Munich would put a UEFA cup place next season beyond all doubt.

Freiburg (17) vs Karlsruhe (7). With a legion of German teams already going forward to Europe next season, Karlsruhe can still ensure their ticket if a victory here allows them to leap ahead of 1860 Munich in sixth place. If not, they have to hope that Stuttgart wins this season's German Cup final, freeing up yet another UEFA place.

Hansa Rostock (14) vs Schalke (13) Back to earth for Schalke after their UEFA victory over Milan with an unglamorous fixture against Rostock, positioned one place below them in the bottom half of the Bundesliga.
Stuttgart (4) vs Arminia Bielefeld (12). Stuttgart's preparations for the German Cup could mean they take the eye off the ball for an encounter at which little is at stake.
Borussia Moenchengladbach (10) vs Bayern Munich (1). Moenchengladbach will hope Bayern, already confirmed as league champions, are resting on their laurels for this clash.
FC St Pauli (18) vs MSV Duisburg (11). A win here for St Pauli could take them off the bottom of the table, if next-to-bottom-placed Freiburg loses.

Borussia Dortmund (3) vs Cologne (9). A test mainly of concentration for Dortmund, playing in front of a home crowd still flush with their team's glorious European Cup victory over holders Juventus on Wednesday
